title: Ransom note on one PC
symptom: Files on the PC have strange extensions and a ransom note has appeared
user_description: All my files have weird names now and there's a text file on my desktop saying I have to pay to get them back! What is happening? Should I restart?

options.text: Restart the PC to see if it goes away
options.why: Restarting does not undo encryption and can destroy evidence the security team needs.

options.text: Disconnect the PC from the network straight away (cable out, Wi-Fi off), do not sign in anywhere else, follow the incident plan and escalate to the security team urgently
options.why: Ransomware can spread to shared drives and other PCs. Cutting the network contains it, and the security team leads the response.

options.text: Restore her files from backup onto the same PC right away
options.why: The infection is still on the PC, so restored files can be encrypted again. Clean-up comes after the security team has investigated.

options.text: Pay the ransom so she can keep working
options.why: Paying does not guarantee the files come back and encourages more attacks. That decision is never made at the help desk.

hints: Could this spread to other computers?
What is the fastest way to cut the PC off from everything else?
Is this something the help desk should handle alone?
real_world_tip: Unless your incident plan says otherwise, many plans say to leave the PC powered on so evidence in memory is kept. Take a photo of the ransom note with your phone.

escalation.team_why: Ransomware is a major security incident. The security team leads the response, checks whether it has spread and decides how to recover.

details.text: When she first noticed the renamed files
details.why: Helps them work out when the attack started and what else to check.

details.text: A photo of the ransom note
details.why: Helps them work out which ransomware this is.

details.text: Which shared drives were mapped on her PC
details.why: Ransomware often encrypts shared drives too, so these need checking fast.

details.text: That the PC is now disconnected from the network
details.why: Tells them it is contained, so they can plan the next step.

details.text: Her password, so they can sign in to her PC
details.why: Never put a password in a ticket. The security team has its own ways in and does not need it.

details.text: The make and model of her monitor
details.why: Has nothing to do with the incident.
